headline: The 10-year climbs past every quarter since 2005
lede: The bond market moved first: the 10-year Treasury closed at 5.24% on 9 October, above every quarterly reading since 2005, a month after the Fed’s first hike since 2023. Prices are still heating, and the S&P 500 is up 14.4% this year.
story: Born out of the 2022 correction, the AI Cycle rode the build-out of artificial intelligence, the story everyone wanted to own. It is a market priced for a boom inside an economy that feels like a slowdown: her valuations sit at the top of the record while her people’s confidence sits at the bottom of it, and the distance between the two is the story of this cycle so far.

elements.weather: Autumn, the stagflation kind. [Temperature](sheet-metric-temp) reads hot at 3.4% and is still heating, while the [Growth gap](sheet-sign-growth-gap) puts output a shade under its potential. The Fed has turned with it: the [Federal funds rate](sheet-sign-hormones) rose a quarter point in September, to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike since 2023. The [S&P 500](sheet-sign-market) has not flinched, up 14.4% this year.
elements.activity: The body is doing more with few new hands. [GDP growth](sheet-metric-gdp) holds a normal pace and [Productivity growth](sheet-sign-productivity-growth) runs above its trend, while [Job growth](sheet-sign-payrolls) has slowed below what her closed cycles usually managed and the [Unemployment rate](sheet-sign-activity) stays low.
elements.mood: Here is the split at the centre of this cycle. The [Buffett indicator](sheet-metric-buffett) stands at 256%, the highest on its record, and [Shiller CAPE](sheet-metric-valuation) is well above its range, yet the market prices in little [Fear](sheet-sign-sentiment). Households read it the other way: [Confidence](sheet-sign-confidence) is a tenth of a point above the record low it set in May.
elements.desire: Shoppers keep spending without leaning on credit: [Discretionary spending](sheet-sign-desire) and [Retail sales](sheet-sign-retail) both sit in their normal ranges. The strain is in the index itself. The ten largest stocks now make up 40.6% of the S&P 500, a [Concentration risk](sheet-sign-concentration) at Risk, and the [Equity risk premium](sheet-sign-premium) has thinned.
elements.circulation: The bond market carries the sharpest reading. The [US 10-year Treasury](sheet-sign-pressure) closed at 5.24% on 9 October, above every quarterly reading since 2005. Money still turns slowly: the [Pulse](sheet-sign-pulse) is weak while [Volume](sheet-sign-volume) holds.
elements.stress: Households carry little debt against their income, but the [Savings rate](sheet-sign-saving) is 2.8%, a thin cushion, and [Margin debt](sheet-sign-margin) is growing faster than its usual range. The heavier load is the state’s: [Federal debt](sheet-metric-debt) is elevated and the [Federal budget](sheet-marker-deficit) runs a large deficit while the economy is still growing.
